  • --output-format, -f: Format to save the import report (json, csv).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To import all data sources from export file my_export.json into ProjectB:

dignacli import-ds ProjectB my_export.json

After the import, this command will also show a report of imported and skipped objects. Only new data sources will be imported into ProjectB. In order to find out which objects would be imported and skipped, you can use the command plan-import-ds

docs.title: plan-import-ds
docs.text: The plan-import-ds command in the digna CLI is used to import data sources into a target project and create an import report.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli plan-import-ds <PROJECT_NAME> <EXPORT_FILE> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project to which the data sources would be imported.
  • EXPORT_FILE: The filename of the data sources export to be analyzed before the import.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --output-file, -o: File to save the import report (if not specified, prints to terminal in tabular form).
  • --output-format, -f: Format to save the import report (json, csv).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To check which data sources would be imported and which would be skipped from export file my_export.json when imported into ProjectB:

dignacli plan-import-ds ProjectB my_export.json

This command will only show an import plan of objects to be imported and skipped.

docs.title: digna CLI Reference 2026.04
docs.text:
2026-04-08

This page documents the full set of commands available in digna CLI release 2026.04, including usage examples and options.

docs.title: help
docs.text:
The --help option provides information about available commands and their usage. There are two main ways to use this option:

  1. Displaying General Help:

    Use –help immediate after the keyword dignacl 

    dignacli --help

  2. Getting Help for Specific Commands:

    For detailed information about a specific command, append --help to that command. For example, to obtain help with the add-user command, run: 

    dignacli add-user --help

    ### output:

    • Command Description: Offers a detailed description of what the command does.
    • Syntax: Shows the exact syntax, including required and optional arguments.
    • Options: Lists any options specific to the command, along with their explanations.
    • Examples: Provides examples of how to execute the command effectively.

docs.title: check-config
docs.text: The check-config command is a utility within the digna CLI tool designed to test the configuration of digna. This command ensures that the digna components can find the needed configuration elements in the config.toml.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: • --configpath, -cp: File or directory that contains the configuration. If omitted, ../config.toml will be used.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text:
dignacli check-config

Upon successful execution, the command outputs a confirmation of completeness of the configration.

If the configuration appears to be incomplete, the missing configuration elements will be listed.

docs.title: check-repo-connection
docs.text: The check-repo-connection command is a utility within the digna CLI tool designed to test the connectivity and access to a specified digna repository. This command ensures that the CLI can interact with the repository.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text:
dignacli check-repo-connection

Upon successful execution, the command outputs a confirmation of the connection, along with details about the repository: Repository version, Host, Database and Schema.

If the repository connection is not successful, check the config.toml file for correct configuration settings.

docs.title: version
docs.text: To check the installed version of dignacli, use the --version option.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli --version

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text: dignacli version 2026.04

docs.title: logging options
docs.text:
By default, the console output of the digna commands is designed to be minimalistic. Most commands offer the possibility of providing additional information, using the following options:

-- verbose (-v) -- debug (-d) -- logfile (lf)

“verbose” and “debug” are defining the level of detail, whereas the “logfile” switch allows redirecting the output to be streamed to a file rather than the console window.

docs.title: add-user
docs.text: The add-user command in the digna CLI is used to add a new user to the digna system

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli add-user [OPTIONS] USER_NAME USER_FULL_NAME USER_PASSWORD

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• USER_NAME: The username for the new user (required).
  • USER_FULL_NAME: The full name of the new user (required).
  • USER_PASSWORD: The password for the new user (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --is_superuser, -su: Flag to designate the new user as an admin.
  • --valid_until, -vu: Sets an expiration date for the user account in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MI:SS. If not set, the account does not have an expiration date.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To add a new user with username jdoe, full name John Doe, and password password123:

dignacli add-user [OPTIONS] USER_NAME USER_FULL_NAME USER_PASSWORD

To add a new user and set an account expiration date: 

dignacli add-user jdoe "John Doe" password123 --valid_until "2024-12-31 23:59:59"

docs.title: delete-user
docs.text: The delete-user command in the digna CLI is used to remove an existing user from the digna system.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli delete-user USER_NAME

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • USER_NAME: The username of the user to be deleted (required). This is the only argument required by the command.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
dignacli delete-user jdoe

Executing this command will remove the user jdoe from the digna system, revoking their access and deleting their associated data and permissions from the repository.

docs.title: modify-user
docs.text: The modify-user command in the digna CLI is used to update the details of an existing user in the digna system.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli modify-user <USER_NAME> <USER_FULL_NAME> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• USER_NAME: The username of the user to be modified (required).
  • USER_FULL_NAME: The new full name for the user (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --is_superuser, -su: Sets the user as a superuser, granting elevated privileges. This flag does not require a value.
  • --valid_until, -vu: Sets an expiration date for the user account in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MI:SS. If not provided, the account remains valid indefinitely.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To modify the full name of the user jdoe to “Johnathan Doe” and set the user as a superuser: 

dignacli modify-user jdoe "Johnathan Doe" --is_superuser

docs.title: modify-user-pwd
docs.text: The modify-user-pwd command in the digna CLI is used to change the password for an existing user in the digna system.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli modify-user-pwd <USER_NAME> <USER_PWD>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• USER_NAME: The username of the user whose password is to be changed (required).
  • USER_PWD: The new password for the user (required).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To change the password for the user jdoe to newpassword123: 

dignacli modify-user-pwd jdoe newpassword123

docs.title: list-users
docs.text: The list-users command in the digna CLI displays a list of all users registered in the digna system.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text:
dignacli list-users

Executing this command in the digna CLI will connect to the digna repository and list all users, showing their ID, username, full name, superuser status, and expiration timestamps.

docs.title: upgrade-repo
docs.text: The upgrade-repo command in the digna CLI is used to upgrade or initialize the digna repository. This command is essential for applying updates or setting up the repository infrastructure for the first time.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli upgrade-repo [options]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: • --simulation-mode, -s: When enabled, this option runs the command in simulation mode, which prints the SQL statements that would be executed but does not actually execute them. This is useful for previewing changes without making any modifications to the repository.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To upgrade the digna repository, you can run the command without any options:

dignacli upgrade-repo
To run the upgrade in simulation mode (to see the SQL statements without applying them):

dignacli upgrade-repo --simulation-mode

This command is crucial for maintaining the digna system, ensuring that the database schema and other repository components are up to date with the latest version of the software.

docs.title: encrypt
docs.text: The encrypt command in the digna CLI is used to encrypt a password.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli encrypt <PASSWORD>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • PASSWORD: The password that needs to be encrypted (required).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To encrypt a password, you need to provide the password as an argument. For instance, to encrypt the password mypassword123, you would use: 

dignacli encrypt mypassword123
This command outputs the encrypted version of the provided password, which can then be used in secure contexts. If the password argument is not provided, the CLI will display an error indicating the missing argument.

docs.title: generate-key
docs.text: The generate-key command is used to generate a Fernet key, which is essential for securing passwords stored in the digna repository.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli generate-key

docs.title: clean-up
docs.text: The clean-up command in the digna CLI is used to remove profiles, predictions, and traffic light system data for one or more data sources within a specified project. This command is essential for data lifecycle management, helping maintain an organized and efficient data environment by clearing outdated or unnecessary data.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli clean-up <PROJECT_NAME> <FROM_DATE> <TO_DATE> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project from which data is to be removed (required). Using the keyword all-projects in this argument instructs digna to iterate over all existing projects and apply this command.
  • FROM_DATE: The start date and time for the data removal. Acceptable formats include %Y-%m-%d, %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S, or %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S (required).
  • TO_DATE: The end date and time for the data removal, following the same formats as FROM_DATE (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --table-name, -tn: Limits the clean-up operation to a specific table within the project.
  • --table-filter, -tf: Filters to limit the clean-up to tables containing the specified substring in their names.
  • --timing, -tm: Displays the time duration of the clean-up process after completion.
  • --help: Displays help information for the clean-up command and exits.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To remove data from the project ProjectA between January 1, 2023, and June 30, 2023:

dignacli clean-up ProjectA 2023-01-01 2023-06-30

To remove data only from a specific table named Table1:

dignacli clean-up ProjectA 2023-01-01 2023-06-30 --table-name Table1

This command helps in managing data storage and ensuring that the repository only contains relevant information.

docs.title: remove-orphans
docs.text: The remove-orphans command in the digna CLI is used for house-keeping in the digna repository. When a user deletes projects or data sources, the profiles and predictions remain in the repository. With this command, such orphaned rows will be removed from the repository.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli list-projects

docs.title: list-projects
docs.text: The list-projects command in the digna CLI is used to display a list of all available projects within the digna system.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text:
dignacli list-projects

This command is especially useful for administrators and users managing multiple projects, providing a quick overview of the available projects in the digna repository.

docs.title: list-ds
docs.text: The list-ds command in the digna CLI is used to display a list of all available data sources within a specified project. This command is useful for understanding the data assets available for analysis and management in the digna system.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli list-ds <PROJECT_NAME>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project for which the data sources are being listed (required).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To list all data sources in the project named ProjectA:

dignacli list-ds ProjectA

This command provides users with an overview of the data sources available in a project, helping them to navigate and manage the data landscape more effectively.

docs.title: inspect
docs.text: The inspect command in the digna CLI is used to create profiles, predictions, and traffic light system data for one or more data sources within a specified project. This command helps in analyzing and monitoring data over a defined period. After completion of the inspection, the value of the calculated traffic light system is returned: - 0: OK - 1: INFO - 2: WARNING

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli inspect <PROJECT_NAME> <FROM_DATE> <TO_DATE> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project for which data is to be inspected (required). Using the keyword all-projects in this argument instructs digna to iterate over all existing projects and apply this command.
  • FROM_DATE: The starting date and time for the data inspection. Acceptable formats include %Y-%m-%d, %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S, or %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S (required).
  • TO_DATE: The ending date and time for the data inspection, following the same formats as FROM_DATE (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --table-name, -tn: Limits the inspection to a specific table within the project.
  • --table-filter, -tf: Filters to inspect only tables containing the specified substring in their names.
  • --enable_notification, -en: Enables the sending of notifications in case of alerts.
  • --bypass-backend, -bb: Bypass backend and run inspection directly from CLI (for testing purposes only!).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To inspect data for the project ProjectA from January 1, 2024, to January 31, 2024:

dignacli inspect ProjectA 2024-01-01 2024-01-31

To inspect only a specific table and force recalculation of predictions:

dignacli inspect ProjectA 2024-01-01 2024-01-31 --table-name Table1 --force-prediction
This command is useful for generating updated profiles and predictions, monitoring data integrity, and managing alert systems within a specified project timeframe.

docs.title: inspect-async
docs.text: The inspect-async command in the digna CLI is used to create profiles, predictions, and traffic light system data for one or more data sources within a specified project. This command helps in analyzing and monitoring data over a defined period. In contrast to the inspect-async command, this does not wait for the completion of the inspection. Instead, it returns the request id for the submitted inspection request. To query the progress of the inspection process, use the command inspect-status

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli inspect-async <PROJECT_NAME> <FROM_DATE> <TO_DATE> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project for which data is to be inspected (required). Using the keyword all-projects in this argument instructs digna to iterate over all existing projects and apply this command.
  • FROM_DATE: The starting date and time for the data inspection. Acceptable formats include %Y-%m-%d, %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S, or %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S (required).
  • TO_DATE: The ending date and time for the data inspection, following the same formats as FROM_DATE (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --table-name, -tn: Limits the inspection to a specific table within the project.
  • --table-filter, -tf: Filters to inspect only tables containing the specified substring in their names.
  • --enable_notification, -en: Enables the sending of notifications in case of alerts.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To inspect data for the project ProjectA from January 1, 2024, to January 31, 2024:

dignacli inspect-async ProjectA 2024-01-01 2024-01-31

docs.title: inspect-status
docs.text: The inspect-status command in the digna CLI is used to check the progress of an asynchronous inspection based on the request ID.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli inspect-status <REQUEST ID>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • REQUEST_ID: The request id returned by the inspect-async command

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To check the progress of an inspection with request ID 12345:

dignacli inspect-status 12345

docs.title: inspect-cancel
docs.text: The inspect-cancel command in the digna CLI is used to cancel inspections based on the request ID or it can be used to cancel all current requests.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text:
dignacli inspect-cancel <REQUEST ID>
dignacli inspect-cancel --killall

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • REQUEST_ID: The request id returned by the inspect-async command

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To cancel the inspection with request ID 12345:

dignacli inspect-cancel 12345

To cancel all requests that are currently running or pending:

dignacli inspect-cancel --killall

docs.title: export-ds
docs.text: The export-ds command in the digna CLI is used to create an export of data sources from the digna repository. By default, all data sources from a given project will be exported.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli export-ds <PROJECT_NAME> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project from which the data sources will be exported.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --table_name, -tn: Export a particular data source from a project.
  • --exportfile, -ef: Specify the filename for the export.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To export all data sources from the project named ProjectA:

dignacli export-ds ProjectA

This command exports all data sources from ProjectA as a JSON document that can be imported to another project or digna repository.

docs.title: import-ds
docs.text: The import-ds command in the digna CLI is used to import data sources into a target project and create an import report.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli import-ds <PROJECT_NAME> <EXPORT_FILE> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project to which the data sources will be imported.
  • EXPORT_FILE: The filename of the data sources export to be imported.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --output-file, -o: File to save the import report (if not specified, prints to terminal in tabular form).
  • --output-format, -f: Format to save the import report (json, csv).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To import all data sources from export file my_export.json into ProjectB:

dignacli import-ds ProjectB my_export.json

After the import, this command will also show a report of imported and skipped objects. Only new data sources will be imported into ProjectB. In order to find out which objects would be imported and skipped, you can use the command plan-import-ds

docs.title: plan-import-ds
docs.text: The plan-import-ds command in the digna CLI is used to import data sources into a target project and create an import report.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli plan-import-ds <PROJECT_NAME> <EXPORT_FILE> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project to which the data sources would be imported.
  • EXPORT_FILE: The filename of the data sources export to be analyzed before the import.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --output-file, -o: File to save the import report (if not specified, prints to terminal in tabular form).
  • --output-format, -f: Format to save the import report (json, csv).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To check which data sources would be imported and which would be skipped from export file my_export.json when imported into ProjectB:

dignacli plan-import-ds ProjectB my_export.json

This command will only show an import plan of objects to be imported and skipped.

docs.title: digna CLI Reference – Introduction | digna Documentation
Purpose of the Command Line Interface (CLI)
docs.text: The digna Command Line Interface (CLI) is a powerful tool designed to streamline interactions with the digna platform. It provides a text-based interface that allows users to perform a wide range of tasks efficiently, without the need for a graphical user interface.

docs.title: Key Features:
docs.text:
• Efficiency and Flexibility: The CLI enables quick execution of commands, improving productivity.
  • Automation: Supports scripting to automate repetitive tasks.
  • Remote Access: Manage digna resources from anywhere.
  • Consistency and Reliability: Ensures reliable operations with documented, version-controlled commands.
  • Scalability: Handles large-scale operations for enterprise tasks.
  • Learning and Mastery: Provides deeper understanding of digna's functionality.
  • Integration with Other Tools: Seamlessly integrates with automation tools like Control-M, UC4, AutomateNOW!

docs.title: Installation Instruction for Windows
docs.text:
To get started, follow the steps outlined below to extract the necessary files, deploy the dignacli folder, and configure your connection to the digna repository. Ensure you have your repository credentials and any required configuration details ready before you begin.

  1. Extracting the digna CLI:
  2. Obtain the .zip file containing the digna CLI.

  3. Unzip the file to your desired directory.

  4. Deploying the dignacli Folder:

  5. Copy the dignacli folder to your preferred installation location (e.g., C:\Program Files\***digna***).

  6. Configuring config.toml:

  7. Check for config.toml inside dignacli.
  8. Rename config_template.toml to config.toml if needed and configure it using the provided documentation.

docs.title: Source Connector for Azure Synapse Analytics
docs.text:
This guide describes how to configure digna to connect to Azure Synapse Analytics using either the native Python connector or the ODBC driver. It supports both serverless and dedicated SQL pools.

This configuration refers to the screen "INTEGRATIONS" → "DB CONNECTIONS" → "+ ADD DB CONNECTION".

docs.title: Native Python Driver
docs.text:
Library: pymssql Supported Authentication: Password-based authentication only

For other authentication methods, please use the ODBC driver.

docs.title: digna Configuration (Native Driver)
docs.text:
Provide the following information in the "Create Database Connection" screen:

Name:               Name of the connection. This is used for referencing the connection in other screens.
Technology:         MS SQL Server
Host Address:       <synapse-workspace>[-ondemand].sql.azuresynapse.net
Host Port:          Port number, e.g. 1433
Database Name:      Database name
User Name:          Database user name
User Password:      Password for the user
Profiling Mode:     The profiling mode determines how digna processes data and calculates metrics:
                    - Standard: Metrics are calculated directly on the source tables without copying the data.
                    - Permanent: Data for the inspected day is copied into a permanent table, and metrics are calculated on the copied data.
                    - Session: Data is copied into a session or temporary table, and metrics are calculated on this temporary data.
                    For serverless SQL pool, only "Standard" is supported.
Work Schema Name:   When using "Permanent" profiling mode, work tables will be placed in this schema.
Use ODBC:           Disabled (default)

docs.title: ODBC Driver
docs.text: The ODBC driver may support a broader range of authentication and connectivity options. This section focuses on password-based authentication using the driver ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server.

docs.title: 1. Install the ODBC Driver
docs.text: Install the driver ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server (or similar) by following the vendor’s official installation guide.

docs.title: 2. Configure the ODBC Data Source
docs.text: Follow these steps to configure a new ODBC data source using password-based authentication:

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text:
Fill out the "Server" field. Use the name of the synapse workspace and extend it with ".sql.azuresynapse.net. Attention, if you want to connect using a serverless SQL pool, make sure to include "-ondemand" as shown in below screenshot.

Click the Next > button.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text:
Choose the authentication method (e.g. username and password) and provide the required data.

Click the Next > button.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Choose the ANSI compliant settings then click the Next > button.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: You can leave the default settings or choose options as needed and click the Finish button.

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: Now click the Test datasource button.

docs.title: Step 6
docs.text:
When you receive the success screen, ODBC is configured properly.

Now you can configure digna to use the ODBC connection, either with a DSN (Data Source Name) or a DSN-less setup.

docs.title: digna Configuration
docs.text:
In the "Create Database Connection" screen, provide the following:

Name:               Name of the connection. This is used for referencing the connection in other screens.
Technology:         MS SQL Server
Database Name:      Database that contains the source schemata
Profiling Mode:     The profiling mode determines how digna processes data and calculates metrics:
                    - Standard: Metrics are calculated directly on the source tables without copying the data.
                    - Permanent: Data for the inspected day is copied into a permanent table, and metrics are calculated on the copied data.
                    - Session: Data is copied into a session or temporary table, and metrics are calculated on this temporary data.
                    For serverless SQL pool, only "Standard" is supported.
Work Schema Name:   When using "Permanent" profiling mode, work tables will be placed in this schema.
Use ODBC:           Enabled

docs.title: ODBC Properties
docs.text:
name: "DSN",        value: "azure-synopse-serverless-1"
name: "UID",        value: "your database user"
name: "PWD",        value: "your database password"
name: "DATABASE",   value: "name of the database that contains the source data schema"

The DSN must match the name defined in your ODBC driver configuration.

docs.title: digna Configuration
docs.text:
In the "Create a Database Connection" screen, provide the following:

Name:               Name of the connection. This is used for referencing the connection in other screens.
Technology:         MS SQL Server
Database Name:      Name of the database that contains the source data schema
Profiling Mode:     The profiling mode determines how digna processes data and calculates metrics:
                    - Standard: Metrics are calculated directly on the source tables without copying the data.
                    - Permanent: Data for the inspected day is copied into a permanent table, and metrics are calculated on the copied data.
                    - Session: Data is copied into a session or temporary table, and metrics are calculated on this temporary data.
                    For serverless SQL pool, only "Standard" is supported.
Work Schema Name:   When using "Permanent" profiling mode, work tables will be placed in this schema.
Use ODBC:           Enabled

docs.title: ODBC Properties
docs.text:
name: "DRIVER",     value: "ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server"
name: "SERVER",     value: "<synapse-workspace>[-ondemand].sql.azuresynapse.net"
name: "UID",        value: "your database user"
name: "PWD",        value: "your database password"
name: "DATABASE",   value: "name of the database that contains the source data schemata"

Note regarding the SERVER property: Use the name of the synapse workspace and extend it with ".sql.azuresynapse.net. If you want to connect using a serverless SQL pool, make sure to include "-ondemand" as shown in below screenshot.

docs.title: Source Connector for Databricks - with Unity Catalog
docs.text:
This guide describes how to configure digna to connect to Databricks using either the native Python connector or the ODBC driver.

It refers to the screen "Create a Database Connection".

docs.title: Native Python Driver
docs.text:
Library: databricks-sql-connector Supported Authentication: Personal Access Token (PAT) only

For other authentication methods, please use the ODBC driver.

docs.title: Personal Access Token (PAT)
docs.text: To authenticate using a personal access token, refer to the official Databricks documentation: How to obtain a PAT

docs.title: digna Configuration (Native Driver)
docs.text:
Provide the following information in the "Create a Database Connection" screen:

Name:               Name of the connection. This is used for referencing the connection in other screens.
Technology:         Databricks
Host Address:       Databricks hostname, e.g. "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx.databricks.com"
Host Port:          e.g. 443
Database Name:      Name of the catalog to use. 
User Name:          HTTP Path provided by Databricks, e.g. "/sql/1.0/warehouses/xxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
User Password:      Personal Access Token, e.g. "dapixxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
Profiling Mode:     The profiling mode determines how digna processes data and calculates metrics:
                    - Standard: Metrics are calculated directly on the source tables without copying the data.
                    - Permanent: Data for the inspected day is copied into a permanent table, and metrics are calculated on the copied data.
                    - Session: Data is copied into a session or temporary table, and metrics are calculated on this temporary data.
Work Schema Name:   When using "Permanent" profiling mode, work tables will be placed in this schema.

docs.title: How to schedule a daily job
docs.text: Scheduling lets you run inspections automatically without manual intervention. In this guide, you’ll learn how to create a job that executes once per day, ensuring that your data is continuously monitored.

docs.title: Interactive Demo
docs.text: Follow the interactive tutorial to see the process in action:

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text:
• How to access the Scheduling section in the digna dashboard
  • How to create a new scheduled job
  • How to configure it to run daily at a fixed time
  • How to select the correct project and datasource
  • How to enable the job so that it runs automatically

docs.title: Why Daily Jobs Are Useful
docs.text:
Daily scheduling is the most common setup in production environments. It ensures:

  • Freshness — every day’s data gets validated.
  • Consistency — anomalies are detected early before they propagate downstream.
  • Automation — no need to manually trigger inspections.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Explore How to use crontab definition for more advanced custom schedules.
  • Combine daily jobs with alerting to get notified when anomalies are detected.

docs.title: Advanced Scheduling with Crontab
docs.text: This guide shows how to schedule jobs in digna using crontab expressions. Unlike the standard patterns (daily, weekly, monthly), crontab gives you full flexibility to define custom schedules.

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text:
• How to open the Scheduling section in the dashboard
  • How to create a new job using a crontab expression
  • How to set a schedule that runs only on weekends at 10:00

docs.title: Example: Weekend Schedule
docs.text:
To schedule a job to run every Saturday and Sunday at 10:00 AM, use the following expression:

  • 0 → minute (on the hour)
  • 10 → hour (10 AM)
  • * → every day of the month
  • * → every month
  • sat,sun → only on Saturdays and Sundays

docs.title: Why Use Crontab?
docs.text:
• Create schedules beyond standard daily, weekly, or monthly patterns
  • Define precise run times (specific days, hours, or intervals)
  • Useful for weekend jobs, off-hours checks, or frequent monitoring

docs.title: Introduction and Overview
docs.text: This guide provides step-by-step instructions for integrating Single Sign-On (SSO) with the digna platform using OpenID Connect (OIDC).

docs.title: What is SSO?
docs.text: Single Sign-On allows users to log in to digna securely using their enterprise credentials through external identity providers. Users can authenticate with their corporate credentials instead of managing separate digna passwords.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
SSO in digna is implemented using the OIDC protocol. Multiple identity providers can be configured in parallel by adjusting two key configuration files:

  • dashboard_config.toml — Controls the frontend login interface
  • config.toml — Configures the backend OIDC connections

docs.title: Supported Providers
docs.text:
Examples in this guide use Microsoft and Google, but any OIDC-compliant provider can be integrated following the same structure.

Common OIDC providers include: - Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) - Google Workspace - Okta - Auth0 - Keycloak - Other OIDC-compliant identity providers

docs.title: Configuration Steps
docs.text: SSO configuration requires updates to two files. This section explains how to configure each one.

docs.title: Overview of Configuration Files
docs.text:
File Location Purpose dashboard_config.toml dashboard/dashboard_config.toml Frontend login interface config.toml /config.toml Backend OIDC connections

Both files must be configured for SSO to work properly.

docs.title: File Location
docs.text: dashboard/dashboard_config.toml

docs.title: Step 1: Add OIDC Providers
docs.text:
Add entries under the [[login.oidc]] array for each identity provider you want to support.

Example with Microsoft and Google:

[[login.oidc]]
key = "microsoft"
label = "Login with Microsoft"

[[login.oidc]]
key = "google"
label = "Login with Google"

docs.title: Step 2: Configure Login Options
docs.text:
Specify whether password-based login should be allowed:

[login]
usePassword = true

docs.title: [[login.oidc]] Section
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description key string Yes Unique identifier for the OIDC connection (must match key in config.toml) label string Yes Text displayed on the login button (e.g., "Login with Microsoft")

docs.title: [login] Section
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description usePassword boolean false Allow password-based login in addition to SSO

docs.title: Understanding usePassword
docs.text:
If usePassword = true: - Login screen shows SSO buttons (e.g., "Login with Microsoft") - Login screen also shows username and password fields - Users can authenticate with either method - Allows hybrid setups where some users use SSO and others use passwords

If usePassword = false (or omitted): - Login screen shows only SSO buttons - No username/password fields - Only OIDC authentication is available

Tip

Password-based login is only available for users who were created with passwords using the digna user add command or via the dashboard.

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
[login]
usePassword = true

[[login.oidc]]
key = "microsoft"
label = "Login with Microsoft"

[[login.oidc]]
key = "google"
label = "Login with Google"

[[login.oidc]]
key = "okta"
label = "Login with Okta"

docs.title: File Location
docs.text:
/config.toml

(Root digna installation directory)

docs.title: Step 1: Add OIDC Provider Sections
docs.text: Each provider must have a dedicated [oidc.<key>] section. The key must match the key defined in dashboard_config.toml.

docs.title: Microsoft Configuration
docs.text:
[oidc.microsoft]
DIGNA_OIDC_CLIENT_ID = "<client_id>"
DIGNA_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET = "<client_secret>"
DIGNA_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI = "http://localhost:5173/oidc/callback"
DIGNA_OIDC_CONFIGURATION_URL = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant_id>/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration"

docs.title: Google Configuration
docs.text:
[oidc.google]
DIGNA_OIDC_CLIENT_ID = "<client_id>"
DIGNA_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET = "<client_secret>"
DIGNA_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI = "http://localhost:5173/oidc/callback"
DIGNA_OIDC_CONFIGURATION_URL = "https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration"

docs.title: Configuration Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description Example DIGNA_OIDC_CLIENT_ID string Yes Client ID from identity provider abc123xyz789 DIGNA_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET string Yes Client secret from identity provider secret_xyz789abc123 DIGNA_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI string Yes Callback URL after authentication http://localhost:5173/oidc/callback DIGNA_OIDC_CONFIGURATION_URL string Yes OIDC configuration endpoint https://login.microsoftonline.com/...

Important

Replace placeholder values (<client_id>, <client_secret>, <tenant_id>) with actual credentials from your identity provider's developer portal.

docs.title: Redirect URI
docs.text:
The redirect URI must be the same in your identity provider configuration:

http://localhost:5173/oidc/callback

If digna is hosted at a different domain, update accordingly: - Local: http://localhost:5173/oidc/callback - Production: https://digna.yourdomain.com/oidc/callback

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
[oidc.microsoft]
DIGNA_OIDC_CLIENT_ID = "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"
DIGNA_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET = "abc123xyz789def456ghi"
DIGNA_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI = "https://digna.yourdomain.com/oidc/callback"
DIGNA_OIDC_CONFIGURATION_URL = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration"

[oidc.google]
DIGNA_OIDC_CLIENT_ID = "123456789-abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz.apps.googleusercontent.com"
DIGNA_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET = "google_secret_xyz789"
DIGNA_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI = "https://digna.yourdomain.com/oidc/callback"
DIGNA_OIDC_CONFIGURATION_URL = "https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration"

docs.title: Testing Login
docs.text: After completing the configuration, verify that SSO is working correctly.

docs.title: Pre-Testing Checklist
docs.text:
Before testing, ensure:

  • dashboard_config.toml has been updated with OIDC providers
  • config.toml has been updated with OIDC credentials
  • Both files have been saved
  • Credentials are correct (client ID, client secret)
  • Redirect URI matches your deployment URL
  • Identity provider application is configured with the redirect URI

docs.title: Step 1: Restart Services
docs.text:
Restart the digna backend and web server to apply changes.

If running as Windows service: 

cd C:\path\to\digna\bin
stop_service.bat
start_service.bat

If running manually: 

cd C:\path\to\digna
digna serve --address localhost --port 8082

If using IIS or Tomcat: Restart your web server service.

docs.title: Step 2: Open Dashboard
docs.text:
Open the digna dashboard in your browser:

http://localhost:5173

(or your configured dashboard URL)

docs.title: Step 3: Verify Login Buttons
docs.text:
Check that login buttons appear for each configured provider:

  • Should see "Login with Microsoft" button
  • Should see "Login with Google" button
  • (If usePassword = true) Should see username/password fields

If buttons don't appear: - Check that dashboard_config.toml was saved - Check that dashboard service was restarted - Check browser console (F12) for errors

docs.title: Step 4: Test SSO Login
docs.text:
Click one of the SSO buttons (e.g., "Login with Microsoft"):

  1. You should be redirected to the identity provider's login page
  2. Log in with your enterprise credentials
  3. You should be redirected back to digna
  4. You should be logged in to digna

docs.title: Step 5: Verify User Creation
docs.text:
After successful SSO login:

  • User should be automatically created in digna
  • User should be logged in
  • User profile should display your identity provider credentials
  • You should see the digna dashboard

docs.title: Step 6: Test Password Login (If Enabled)
docs.text:
If usePassword = true:

  1. Log out of digna
  2. On the login page, enter a username and password
  3. You should be able to log in with password credentials

docs.title: Login Buttons Don't Appear
docs.text:
Symptoms: - OIDC login buttons not visible on login page - Only see password fields (if usePassword = true)

Causes & Solutions: 1. Check dashboard_config.toml is in dashboard/ directory 2. Verify [[login.oidc]] sections are present with correct syntax 3. Restart dashboard service 4. Clear browser cache (Ctrl+Shift+Delete or Cmd+Shift+Delete) 5. Check browser console (F12 → Console tab) for errors

docs.title: Redirect URI Mismatch Error
docs.text:
Symptoms: - After clicking SSO button, error about "redirect_uri mismatch" - "The redirect URI is not registered" error

Causes & Solutions: 1. Verify DIGNA_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI in config.toml is correct 2. Verify redirect URI is registered in identity provider settings 3. Ensure both use identical URLs (including protocol, domain, path) 4. Check for typos in the redirect URI 5. If using HTTPS, ensure certificate is valid

docs.title: Invalid Client Credentials Error
docs.text:
Symptoms: - "Invalid client ID or secret" error - Authentication fails with credentials error

Causes & Solutions: 1. Verify DIGNA_OIDC_CLIENT_ID and DIGNA_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET are correct 2. Ensure no extra spaces or special characters 3. Check credentials haven't expired or been revoked 4. Restart backend service after updating config 5. Check identity provider console to confirm credentials are active

docs.title: Login Hangs or Times Out
docs.text:
Symptoms: - Clicking SSO button does nothing - Timeout after several seconds - Browser shows "Failed to connect" or similar

Causes & Solutions: 1. Verify digna backend is running: digna repo check 2. Check network connectivity to identity provider 3. Verify DIGNA_OIDC_CONFIGURATION_URL is accessible 4. Check firewall rules allow outbound HTTPS connections 5. Verify backend and dashboard can reach each other

docs.title: Users Not Automatically Created
docs.text:
Symptoms: - SSO login succeeds but user not created in digna - Get permission error after SSO login

Causes & Solutions: 1. Verify OIDC configuration is correct 2. Check user permissions are set up 3. Review digna logs for error messages 4. Restart backend service 5. Contact support@digna.ai if issue persists

docs.title: Tested & Supported
docs.text:
The following OIDC providers have been tested and are known to work:

Provider Configuration URL Setup Guide Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant_id>/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration Microsoft Doc Google Workspace https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration Google Doc Okta https://<domain>/.well-known/openid-configuration Okta Doc

docs.title: Other OIDC Providers
docs.text:
Any provider that supports OpenID Connect can be integrated. Required information:

  • Client ID
  • Client secret
  • OpenID configuration URL (usually at /.well-known/openid-configuration)
  • Supported scopes (typically openid profile email)

Contact support@digna.ai if you need help integrating a specific provider.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
DO: - Use HTTPS in production (not HTTP) - Store client secrets securely (use environment variables if possible) - Rotate secrets periodically - Test in a non-production environment first - Document which providers are configured - Monitor login logs for unusual activity - Keep identity provider configuration in sync with digna config

DON'T: - Store client secrets in version control - Use HTTP redirect URIs in production - Configure multiple providers with the same key - Leave default/test credentials in production - Expose config files containing secrets - Mix development and production credentials

docs.text:
Need help with SSO configuration?

  • Email: support@digna.ai
  • Documentation: https://docs.digna.ai
  • Website: https://www.digna.ai

docs.title: About digna
docs.text:
digna is a comprehensive AI-driven platform designed to optimize data quality management across various data environments such as warehouses, lakes, and lakehouses. Built to be highly scalable and adaptable, digna addresses modern data challenges through automation, real-time monitoring, and anomaly detection.

digna consists of two main components:

  • dignabackend: The core engine of the application, responsible for processing data and performing quality checks.
  • dignadashboard: A web-based interface hosted on a web server, providing a user-friendly way to interact with the digna platform and visualize data quality metrics.

docs.title: What's New in Release 2026.06
docs.text: This release brings data observability capabilities directly into your code, enabling developers to monitor data quality at the source. See the release notes for complete details.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
Before you begin the installation, ensure that your system meets the following minimum requirements:

Requirement Specification Operating System Windows Server or Windows 10/11 Memory (Minimal Setup) 16 GB RAM Disk Space 10 GB available storage Database PostgreSQL Server 12 or higher Web Server IIS, Apache Tomcat, or equivalent

docs.title: Database Installation Options
docs.text:
If PostgreSQL is already installed: You can add a new database for digna to your existing PostgreSQL Server.

If installing PostgreSQL on the same machine as digna:

Recommended Specifications

  • Memory: 32 GB RAM (instead of 16 GB)
  • Disk Space: 50 GB available storage (instead of 10 GB)

These higher specifications accommodate both digna and the PostgreSQL database running simultaneously.

docs.title: Pre-Installation Setup
docs.text:
Before installing digna, ensure that two key prerequisites are in place:

  1. PostgreSQL Server – for storing calculated metrics and performance data
  2. Web Server – for hosting the digna Dashboard

If these components are not already set up, follow the sections below to install and configure them.

docs.title: If You Already Have PostgreSQL
docs.text: If PostgreSQL is already installed and running on your local machine or if you are using a managed remote PostgreSQL server, you can skip to the next section.

docs.title: Installing PostgreSQL
docs.text: Follow these steps to install PostgreSQL on Windows:

docs.title: Step 1: Download PostgreSQL
docs.text:
1. Visit the PostgreSQL Downloads page
  2. Select Windows
  3. Download the latest installer

docs.title: Step 2: Run the Installer
docs.text:
1. Double-click the downloaded installer file
  2. Follow the prompts in the setup wizard

docs.title: Step 3: Choose Installation Directory
docs.text: Select the directory where PostgreSQL will be installed. The default location is usually appropriate.

docs.title: Step 4: Select Components
docs.text: For a standard setup, keep the default component options selected.

docs.title: Step 5: Set PostgreSQL Superuser Password
docs.text: Enter and confirm a password for the PostgreSQL superuser (postgres). Save this password securely — you will need it later.

docs.title: Step 6: Configure Port Number
docs.text:
The default PostgreSQL port is 5432. You can use the default or specify a different port if needed.

Tip

If port 5432 is already in use, choose an alternative port and note it for later configuration.

docs.title: Step 7: Choose Locale
docs.text: Select the locale for your database. The default is usually suitable for most installations.

docs.title: Step 8: Complete Installation
docs.text: Click Next through the remaining steps, then click Finish.

docs.title: Step 9: Verify Installation
docs.text:
Open Command Prompt and verify PostgreSQL is installed:

psql --version

You should see the PostgreSQL version if the installation was successful.

docs.title: Web Server Configuration
docs.text:
digna requires a web server to host the dashboard. Choose one of the following options:

  • Internet Information Services (IIS)
  • Apache Tomcat

You only need to install and configure one of these servers.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Internet Information Services (IIS) is Microsoft's web server for hosting websites and web applications.

docs.title: Enabling IIS
docs.text:
1. Open Control Panel
  2. Press Win + R

  3. Type control and press Enter

  4. Navigate to Windows Features

  5. Click Programs

  6. Select Turn Windows features on or off

  7. Enable Internet Information Services

  8. Scroll down and find Internet Information Services (IIS)
  9. Check the checkbox to enable it

  10. Click the + to expand and verify these subcomponents are selected:

    • Web Management Tools
    • World Wide Web Services

  11. Click OK to apply changes

  12. Verify IIS Installation

  13. Open your browser
  14. Navigate to http://localhost
  15. You should see the IIS Welcome page

docs.title: Required: URL Rewrite Module
docs.text: IIS requires the URL Rewrite component. Download and install it from the official Microsoft page.

docs.title: Required: MIME Type for Markdown Files
docs.text:
To ensure Markdown files (.md) are served correctly by IIS:

  1. Open IIS Manager (press Win + R, type inetmgr, press Enter)
  2. Navigate to Your Site > MIME Types
  3. Click Add...
  4. Configure:
  5. File name extension: .md
  6. MIME type: text/markdown

Important

Without this setting, .md files may not be served properly.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Apache Tomcat is an open-source Java servlet container and web server.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Download Apache Tomcat
  2. Visit Apache Tomcat Downloads

  3. Download the Windows ZIP distribution

  4. Extract the Archive

  5. Extract the ZIP file to a directory on your system

  6. Example: C:\Program Files\Apache Tomcat

  7. Verify Tomcat is Running

  8. Open your browser
  9. Navigate to http://localhost:8080
  10. You should see the Apache Tomcat welcome page

Tip

Apache Tomcat typically starts automatically after installation. If it doesn't, navigate to the bin folder and run startup.bat.

docs.title: Step 1: Set Up the digna Repository
docs.text: The digna repository stores all metrics calculated by digna. It acts as the central database for analytical and performance data.

docs.title: Create Repository Schema and User
docs.text:
Open your PostgreSQL client (pgAdmin, psql, or similar) and execute the following SQL commands:

CREATE SCHEMA <digna_repo_schema>;

CREATE USER <digna_repo_user> WITH PASSWORD '<digna_repo_password>';

GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON SCHEMA <digna_repo_schema> TO <digna_repo_user>;

Replace the following placeholders:

  • <digna_repo_schema> — Your desired schema name (e.g., dignarepo)
  • <digna_repo_user> — Your desired username (e.g., digna_user)
  • <digna_repo_password> — A secure password for this user

Example:

CREATE SCHEMA dignarepo;

CREATE USER digna_user WITH PASSWORD 'YourSecurePassword123!';

GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON SCHEMA dignarepo TO digna_user;

Best Practice

Use strong, complex passwords for database users. Avoid easily guessable credentials.

docs.title: Step 2: Extract the digna Installation Package
docs.text:
1. Locate the digna installation ZIP file provided to you
  2. Extract it to your desired installation location
  3. After extraction, you should see the following items:
  4. dashboard/ — Web dashboard interface
  5. digna — Main executable (backend + CLI combined)
  6. config.toml — Configuration file
  7. license.toml — License file (copy yours here)

docs.title: Step 3: Install the License File
docs.text:
Important

The license file is not included in the installation package and will be provided separately by digna.

  1. Locate the license.toml file provided to you
  2. Copy it into the root digna installation directory (where config.toml and the digna executable are located)

Why this matters: The license file contains your customer information, license expiration date, and digital signature. Do not modify this file — any changes will invalidate it.

Directory structure after setup:

digna_installation/
├── config.toml         (configuration file)
├── license.toml        (YOUR LICENSE FILE - copy here)
├── digna               (main executable)
└── dashboard/          (web interface)
    └── (dashboard files)

docs.title: Step 1: Create and Edit the Configuration File
docs.text:
The config_template.toml file is provided in your digna installation directory. You only need to rename it to config.toml.

Location: digna_installation/config.toml

Open config.toml in a text editor and configure each section below.

docs.title: [app] Section
docs.text:
This section configures the digna backend application settings:

[app]
digna_APP_HOST = "localhost"
digna_APP_PORT = 8082
digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS = ["http://localhost:5173"]
digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS = true
digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_METHODS = ["*"]
digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_HEADERS = ["*"]
Parameter Value Notes digna_APP_HOST localhost or IP address Hostname or IP where dignabackend is hosted digna_APP_PORT 8082 (default) Port for REST API endpoints digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS Frontend URL If dashboard is on different server, include its URL digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS true Required for CORS with credentials digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_METHODS ["*"] Allow all HTTP methods digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_HEADERS ["*"] Allow all headers

docs.title: [repo] Section
docs.text:
This section configures the connection to the PostgreSQL database:

[repo]
digna_REPO_HOST = "localhost"
digna_REPO_PORT = 5432
digna_REPO_DB = "postgres"
digna_REPO_SCHEMA = "dignarepo"
digna_REPO_USER = "digna_user"
digna_REPO_PASSWORD = "YourSecurePassword123!"
Parameter Value Notes digna_REPO_HOST localhost or IP PostgreSQL server hostname/IP digna_REPO_PORT 5432 (default) PostgreSQL port digna_REPO_DB postgres Database name digna_REPO_SCHEMA dignarepo Schema created earlier digna_REPO_USER digna_user User created in PostgreSQL setup digna_REPO_PASSWORD Your password Password set during schema creation

docs.title: [base] Section
docs.text:
This section contains security and cookie settings:

[base]
digna_FERNET_KEY = "your-fernet-key"
digna_COOKIE_DOMAIN = "localhost"
digna_COOKIE_PATH = "/"
digna_COOKIE_SECURE = false
digna_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = true
digna_COOKIE_SAME_SITE = "lax"
digna_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN = 86400
digna_MAX_WORKERS = 4
Parameter Value Notes digna_FERNET_KEY Encryption key Used to encrypt tokens and cookies (default provided) digna_COOKIE_DOMAIN localhost Match your frontend domain digna_COOKIE_SECURE false (local) / true (production) Use true for HTTPS connections digna_COOKIE_HTTPONLY true Always enabled for security digna_COOKIE_SAME_SITE lax Prevents CSRF attacks digna_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN 86400 (24 hours) Session timeout in seconds digna_MAX_WORKERS Number of CPU cores - 1 Number of parallel inspection tasks

docs.title: [logging] Section
docs.text:
This section configures logging behavior:

[logging]
digna_LOGGING_MODE = "INFO"
digna_LOGGING_BACKUP_COUNT = 10
Parameter Value Notes digna_LOGGING_MODE INFO or DEBUG INFO for production, DEBUG for troubleshooting digna_LOGGING_BACKUP_COUNT 10 Number of daily log backups to retain

docs.title: Step 3: Initialize the Repository
docs.text:
1. Open Command Prompt
  2. Navigate to your digna installation directory (where config.toml and the digna executable are located)
  3. Run the connection test:
digna repo check

You should see a confirmation that the connection is established (the repository itself hasn't been initialized yet).

docs.title: Step 4: Install the Repository Schema
docs.text:
In the same directory, run:

digna repo install

This command installs the necessary tables and schema in your PostgreSQL database.

docs.title: Step 5: Start the digna Server
docs.text:
In the digna installation directory, start the server with:

digna serve --address <host> --port <port>

Parameters: - --address — Server hostname/IP - --port — Server port

You should see startup messages confirming the server is running:

INFO:     Started server process [1234]
INFO:     Waiting for application startup.
INFO:     Application startup complete
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://localhost:8082

docs.title: Step 6: Create an Admin User
docs.text:
1. Open a new Command Prompt window
  2. Navigate to your digna installation directory
  3. Run the following command to create an admin user:
digna user add <username> "<full_name>" <password> --su

Example:

digna user add admin "Admin User" AdminPassword123! --su

This creates a user with full administrative privileges.

Best Practice

Use a strong password with a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters.

docs.title: Step 1: Deploy Dashboard to Web Server
docs.text:
The digna dashboard has its own separate config.toml file located in the dashboard/ directory. This configuration is already provided and does not require changes during initial setup. You only need to configure it if you need to customize the backend connection.

If you need to modify the dashboard configuration (e.g., for multi-instance deployments), refer to the dashboard's documentation.

Choose your web server and follow the corresponding deployment steps.

docs.title: Deploying to IIS
docs.text:
1. Open IIS Manager

  2. Press Win + R, type inetmgr, press Enter

  3. Create a New Website

  4. In the left panel, right-click Sites

  5. Select Add Website...

  6. Configure the Website

  7. Site Name: Enter a name (e.g., "dignaDashboard")
  8. Physical Path: Click Browse and select your dashboard folder

  9. Binding: Set IP address and port (default port 80 for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS)

  10. Start the Website

  11. Click OK to create the site

  12. Right-click the new site and select Start

  13. Test the Installation

  14. Open your browser
  15. Navigate to http://localhost (or your configured URL)
  16. You should see the digna dashboard login page

docs.title: Deploying to Apache Tomcat
docs.text:
1. Copy Dashboard to Tomcat
  2. Copy the dashboard folder to your Tomcat webapps directory
  3. Rename it if needed (e.g., to digna)

  4. Example: C:\Program Files\Apache Tomcat\webapps\digna

  5. Verify Deployment

  6. Refresh or reload the Tomcat management page (http://localhost:8080)

  7. You should see "digna" (or your chosen name) listed in the deployed applications

  8. Access the Dashboard

  9. Open your browser
  10. Navigate to http://localhost:8080/digna
  11. You should see the digna dashboard login page

docs.title: Running digna as a Windows Service
Why Use a Windows Service?
docs.text: Running the digna backend as a Windows service ensures it: - Starts automatically when the server boots - Runs in the background without an open Command Prompt - Restarts automatically if it crashes - Can be managed through Windows Services

docs.title: Service Management Files
docs.text:
All necessary files are located in the digna installation directory under: bin/

The following batch files are available: - install_service.bat — Registers digna as a Windows service - uninstall_service.bat — Unregisters the service - start_service.bat — Starts the running service - stop_service.bat — Stops the running service

Administrator Required

All batch files must be executed with Administrator privileges.

docs.title: Installing the Service
docs.text:
1. Open Command Prompt as Administrator
  2. Right-click Command Prompt

  3. Select "Run as Administrator"

  4. Navigate to the bin Folder 

    cd C:\path\to\digna\bin

  5. Run the Installation Script 

    install_service.bat

The digna server is now registered as a Windows service with automatic startup enabled. The service does not start immediately — see the next section to start it.

docs.title: To Start the Service
docs.text:
1. Open Command Prompt as Administrator
  2. Navigate to digna\bin
  3. Run: 
    start_service.bat

docs.title: To Stop the Service
docs.text:
1. Open Command Prompt as Administrator
  2. Navigate to digna\bin
  3. Run: 
    stop_service.bat

Tip

Always stop the service before updating application files.

docs.title: Moving the Service to a New Directory
docs.text:
If you need to relocate the digna installation:

  1. Uninstall the Current Service 

    cd C:\old\path\digna\bin
uninstall_service.bat

  2. Move the Application Files

  3. Move the entire digna installation folder to the new location

  4. Reinstall the Service 

    cd C:\new\path\digna\bin
install_service.bat

  5. Start the Service 

    start_service.bat

docs.title: Uninstalling the Service
docs.text:
1. Stop the Running Service 

    cd C:\path\to\digna\bin
stop_service.bat

  2. Uninstall the Service 

    uninstall_service.bat

The digna server is now unregistered as a Windows service.

docs.title: Before You Upgrade
docs.text:
Creating a digna Repository Backup is Mandatory

Before upgrading digna, back up your repository (PostgreSQL) to protect against data loss. A backup ensures you can recover if the upgrade encounters unexpected issues.

docs.title: Step 1: Stop digna Service
docs.text:
If digna is running as a Windows service, stop it first:

cd C:\path\to\digna\bin
stop_service.bat

docs.title: Step 2: Backup Current Backend Installation
docs.text:
In your digna installation directory:

# Rename folder containing dignabackend
ren dignabackend dignabackend_old

# Rename dashboard
ren dashboard dashboard_old

docs.title: Step 3: Extract and Deploy New Version
docs.text:
1. Extract the new digna installation ZIP file
  2. Copy the new digna executable, dashboard folder to your installation directory

Important

The config.toml file is never included in the installation ZIP. Your existing configuration remains safe.

docs.title: Step 4: Restore Your Configuration Files
docs.text: copy dashboard_old\dashboard_config.toml dashboard\dashboard_config.toml

docs.title: Step 5: Upgrade the Repository Schema
docs.text:
Navigate to your digna installation directory and run:

digna repo upgrade

This updates the PostgreSQL schema to the latest version while preserving all existing data.

docs.title: Step 6: Restart Services
docs.text:
If running as a Windows service:

cd C:\path\to\digna\bin
start_service.bat

If running manually, restart the server:

cd C:\path\to\digna
digna serve --address <address> --port <port>

If using IIS or Tomcat, restart the respective web server.

docs.title: Step 7: Verify the Upgrade
docs.text:
1. Access the digna dashboard
  2. Verify that the interface loads correctly
  3. Check the server logs for any errors

docs.title: macOS Installation Guide for digna Release 2026.06
docs.text:
Release: 2026.06

Last Updated: September 5, 2026

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
1. Introduction
  2. System Requirements
  3. Pre-Installation Setup
  4. PostgreSQL Server Setup
  5. Web Server Configuration
  6. Initial Installation
  7. Backend Configuration
  8. Dashboard Configuration
  9. Running digna as a Background Service
  10. Upgrading to a New Release

docs.title: About digna
docs.text:
digna is a comprehensive AI-driven platform designed to optimize data quality management across various data environments such as warehouses, lakes, and lakehouses. Built to be highly scalable and adaptable, digna addresses modern data challenges through automation, real-time monitoring, and anomaly detection.

digna consists of two main components:

  • dignabackend: The core engine of the application, responsible for processing data and performing quality checks.
  • dignadashboard: A web-based interface hosted on a web server, providing a user-friendly way to interact with the digna platform and visualize data quality metrics.

docs.title: What's New in Release 2026.06
docs.text: This release brings data observability capabilities directly into your code, enabling developers to monitor data quality at the source. See the release notes for complete details.

docs.title: Looking for Windows?
docs.text: This guide covers macOS. For a Windows Server or Windows 10/11 installation, see the Windows Installation Guide.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
Before you begin the installation, ensure that your system meets the following minimum requirements:

Requirement Specification Operating System macOS 13 (Ventura) or later Architecture Apple Silicon (arm64) or Intel (x86_64) Memory (Minimal Setup) 16 GB RAM Disk Space 10 GB available storage Database PostgreSQL Server 12 or higher Web Server nginx, Apache httpd, or equivalent Command Line Tools Xcode Command Line Tools (required by Homebrew)

docs.title: Database Installation Options
docs.text:
If PostgreSQL is already installed: You can add a new database for digna to your existing PostgreSQL Server.

If installing PostgreSQL on the same machine as digna:

Recommended Specifications

  • Memory: 32 GB RAM (instead of 16 GB)
  • Disk Space: 50 GB available storage (instead of 10 GB)

These higher specifications accommodate both digna and the PostgreSQL database running simultaneously.

docs.title: Checking Your Architecture
docs.text:
Several paths in this guide differ between Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. To check which you have, open Terminal and run:

uname -m
  • arm64 — Apple Silicon. Homebrew installs to /opt/homebrew.
  • x86_64 — Intel. Homebrew installs to /usr/local.

Tip

Rather than hard-coding either path, this guide uses $(brew --prefix), which expands to the correct location on both architectures. You can copy the commands verbatim.

docs.title: Pre-Installation Setup
docs.text:
Before installing digna, ensure that three key prerequisites are in place:

  1. Homebrew – the package manager used to install the components below
  2. PostgreSQL Server – for storing calculated metrics and performance data
  3. Web Server – for hosting the digna Dashboard

If these components are not already set up, follow the sections below to install and configure them.

docs.title: Installing Homebrew
docs.text: Homebrew is the standard package manager for macOS and is used throughout this guide to install PostgreSQL and nginx.

docs.title: Step 1: Check Whether Homebrew Is Already Installed
docs.text:
Open Terminal (press Cmd + Space, type Terminal, press Enter) and run:

brew --version

If a version number is returned, skip to the PostgreSQL Server Setup section.

docs.title: Step 2: Install Homebrew
docs.text: If the command was not found, install Homebrew by following the instructions on the official Homebrew site. The installer also installs the Xcode Command Line Tools if they are not already present.

docs.title: Step 3: Add Homebrew to Your PATH
docs.text:
On Apple Silicon, the installer prints two commands to add Homebrew to your shell environment. Run them as instructed, then confirm:

brew --prefix

This should print /opt/homebrew on Apple Silicon or /usr/local on Intel.

docs.title: If You Already Have PostgreSQL
docs.text: If PostgreSQL is already installed and running on your local machine or if you are using a managed remote PostgreSQL server, you can skip to the next section.

docs.title: Installation Options
docs.text:
macOS offers two straightforward ways to install PostgreSQL. Choose one:

  • Homebrew — command-line installation, recommended for server deployments
  • Postgres.app — graphical installation, convenient for local evaluation

docs.title: Step 1: Install the PostgreSQL Formula
docs.text: brew install postgresql@16

docs.title: Step 2: Add PostgreSQL to Your PATH
docs.text:
Versioned PostgreSQL formulas are keg-only, which means Homebrew does not link their commands into your PATH automatically. Add them yourself:

echo 'export PATH="'$(brew --prefix)'/opt/postgresql@16/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc

Note

This assumes the default zsh shell used by macOS. If you use bash, append the same line to ~/.bash_profile instead.

docs.title: Step 3: Start the PostgreSQL Service
docs.text:
brew services start postgresql@16

This starts PostgreSQL immediately and configures it to start again automatically when you log in.

docs.title: Step 4: Verify the Installation
docs.text:
psql --version

You should see the PostgreSQL version if the installation was successful.

docs.title: Step 5: Connect to the Server
docs.text:
psql postgres

Important — macOS Differs From Windows Here

The Windows installer prompts you to create a postgres superuser and password. Homebrew does not. Instead it creates a superuser named after your macOS account, with no password, reachable only from the local machine.

This means there is no postgres role on a fresh Homebrew installation. Use your own account name when you need a superuser, and create an explicit digna user as described in Initial Installation.

docs.title: Step 6: Confirm the Port
docs.text:
The default PostgreSQL port is 5432. To confirm the port your server is listening on:

psql postgres -c "SHOW port;"

Note the value — you will need it when configuring the digna backend.

docs.title: Installing PostgreSQL with Postgres.app
docs.text:
If you prefer a graphical installation:

  1. Download Postgres.app and drag it into your Applications folder
  2. Open the app and click Initialize to create a new server
  3. Follow the app's instructions to add its command-line tools to your PATH
  4. Verify the installation:
psql --version

Postgres.app also creates a superuser named after your macOS account.

docs.title: Web Server Configuration
docs.text:
digna requires a web server to host the dashboard. Choose one of the following options:

  • nginx — installed via Homebrew, recommended
  • Apache httpd — included with macOS

You only need to install and configure one of these servers.

Both sections configure two things the dashboard depends on:

  • A single-page-application fallback, so that refreshing a dashboard URL does not return a 404
  • A .md MIME type, so that Markdown files are served correctly

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: nginx is a lightweight, high-performance web server well suited to serving the static digna dashboard.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: brew install nginx

docs.title: Starting nginx
docs.text: brew services start nginx

docs.title: Verify the Installation
docs.text:
1. Open your browser
  2. Navigate to http://localhost:8080
  3. You should see the nginx welcome page

Note — Default Port Is 8080, Not 80

Homebrew configures nginx to listen on port 8080 so that it can run without administrator privileges. On macOS, binding to port 80 or any other port below 1024 requires root.

To serve the dashboard on port 80, change listen 8080; to listen 80; in the configuration below and start nginx with sudo brew services start nginx instead.

docs.title: Configuring a Site for the Dashboard
docs.text:
Homebrew's nginx configuration includes every file in its servers directory. Create a dedicated configuration file for digna there:

nano $(brew --prefix)/etc/nginx/servers/digna.conf

Paste the following, replacing /path/to/digna/dashboard with the actual path to your extracted dashboard folder:

server {
    listen       8080;
    server_name  localhost;

    root   /path/to/digna/dashboard;
    index  index.html;

    # Serve Markdown files with the correct MIME type.
    types {
        text/markdown  md;
    }

    # Single-page-application fallback: unknown paths return index.html
    # instead of a 404, so dashboard routes survive a browser refresh.
    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
    }
}

Important

Without the try_files directive, reloading any dashboard page other than the root URL returns a 404. This is the nginx equivalent of the URL Rewrite module required by IIS on Windows.

docs.title: Apply the Configuration
docs.text:
Test the configuration for syntax errors, then reload nginx:

nginx -t
brew services restart nginx

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: macOS includes Apache httpd, so no installation is required. It is disabled by default.

docs.title: Starting Apache
docs.text: sudo apachectl start

docs.title: Verify the Installation
docs.text:
1. Open your browser
  2. Navigate to http://localhost
  3. You should see the message "It works!"

docs.title: Required: Enable mod_rewrite
docs.text:
The dashboard requires URL rewriting. Open the Apache configuration:

sudo nano /etc/apache2/httpd.conf

Find the following line and remove the leading # to uncomment it:

LoadModule rewrite_module libexec/apache2/mod_rewrite.so

docs.title: Required: Allow .htaccess Overrides
docs.text:
In the same file, locate the <Directory "/Library/WebServer/Documents"> block and change:

AllowOverride None

to:

AllowOverride All

docs.title: Required: MIME Type for Markdown Files
docs.text:
Still in httpd.conf, add the following line so that Markdown files are served correctly:

AddType text/markdown .md

Important

Without this setting, .md files may not be served properly.

docs.title: Apply the Configuration
docs.text:
Check the configuration for syntax errors, then restart Apache:

sudo apachectl configtest
sudo apachectl restart

docs.title: Step 1: Set Up the digna Repository
docs.text: The digna repository stores all metrics calculated by digna. It acts as the central database for analytical and performance data.

docs.title: Create Repository Schema and User
docs.text:
Open your PostgreSQL client (psql, pgAdmin, or similar) and execute the following SQL commands:

CREATE SCHEMA <digna_repo_schema>;

CREATE USER <digna_repo_user> WITH PASSWORD '<digna_repo_password>';

GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON SCHEMA <digna_repo_schema> TO <digna_repo_user>;

Replace the following placeholders:

  • <digna_repo_schema> — Your desired schema name (e.g., dignarepo)
  • <digna_repo_user> — Your desired username (e.g., digna_user)
  • <digna_repo_password> — A secure password for this user

Example:

CREATE SCHEMA dignarepo;

CREATE USER digna_user WITH PASSWORD 'YourSecurePassword123!';

GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON SCHEMA dignarepo TO digna_user;

To run these from the Terminal in a single step:

psql postgres

Then paste the statements at the postgres=# prompt and type \q to exit.

Best Practice

Use strong, complex passwords for database users. Avoid easily guessable credentials.

docs.title: Step 2: Extract the digna Installation Package
docs.text:
1. Locate the digna installation ZIP file provided to you
  2. Extract it to your desired installation location — for example /opt/digna or ~/digna
  3. After extraction, you should see the following items:
  4. dashboard/ — Web dashboard interface
  5. digna — Main executable (backend + CLI combined)
  6. config.toml — Configuration file
  7. license.toml — License file (copy yours here)

To extract from the Terminal:

unzip digna-2026.06-macos.zip -d /opt/digna

docs.title: Make the Executable Runnable
docs.text:
Depending on how the archive was transferred, the executable bit may not survive extraction. Set it explicitly:

cd /opt/digna
chmod +x digna

docs.title: If macOS Blocks the Application
docs.text:
Files downloaded through a browser or mail client are tagged with a quarantine attribute. If macOS reports that the app "cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified", clear the attribute from the installation directory:

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /opt/digna

Alternatively, open System Settings → Privacy & Security, find the blocked item near the bottom of the page, and click Open Anyway.

Note

This step is only needed if macOS actually blocks the executable. Packages transferred over SSH or from internal file shares are usually not quarantined.

docs.title: Step 3: Install the License File
docs.text:
Important

The license file is not included in the installation package and will be provided separately by digna.

  1. Locate the license.toml file provided to you
  2. Copy it into the root digna installation directory (where config.toml and the digna executable are located)

Why this matters: The license file contains your customer information, license expiration date, and digital signature. Do not modify this file — any changes will invalidate it.

Directory structure after setup:

/opt/digna/
├── config.toml         (configuration file)
├── license.toml        (YOUR LICENSE FILE - copy here)
├── digna               (main executable)
├── bin/                (service management scripts)
└── dashboard/          (web interface)
    └── (dashboard files)

docs.title: Step 1: Create and Edit the Configuration File
docs.text:
The config_template.toml file is provided in your digna installation directory. You only need to rename it to config.toml.

cd /opt/digna
mv config_template.toml config.toml

Location: /opt/digna/config.toml

Open config.toml in a text editor and configure each section below.

docs.title: [app] Section
docs.text:
This section configures the digna backend application settings:

[app]
digna_APP_HOST = "localhost"
digna_APP_PORT = 8082
digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS = ["http://localhost:5173"]
digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS = true
digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_METHODS = ["*"]
digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_HEADERS = ["*"]
Parameter Value Notes digna_APP_HOST localhost or IP address Hostname or IP where dignabackend is hosted digna_APP_PORT 8082 (default) Port for REST API endpoints digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS Frontend URL If dashboard is on different server, include its URL digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS true Required for CORS with credentials digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_METHODS ["*"] Allow all HTTP methods digna_APP_CORS_ALLOW_HEADERS ["*"] Allow all headers

Note

If you serve the dashboard from Homebrew's nginx on its default port, the origin to allow is http://localhost:8080.

docs.title: [repo] Section
docs.text:
This section configures the connection to the PostgreSQL database:

[repo]
digna_REPO_HOST = "localhost"
digna_REPO_PORT = 5432
digna_REPO_DB = "postgres"
digna_REPO_SCHEMA = "dignarepo"
digna_REPO_USER = "digna_user"
digna_REPO_PASSWORD = "YourSecurePassword123!"
Parameter Value Notes digna_REPO_HOST localhost or IP PostgreSQL server hostname/IP digna_REPO_PORT 5432 (default) PostgreSQL port digna_REPO_DB postgres Database name digna_REPO_SCHEMA dignarepo Schema created earlier digna_REPO_USER digna_user User created in PostgreSQL setup digna_REPO_PASSWORD Your password Password set during schema creation

docs.title: [base] Section
docs.text:
This section contains security and cookie settings:

[base]
digna_FERNET_KEY = "your-fernet-key"
digna_COOKIE_DOMAIN = "localhost"
digna_COOKIE_PATH = "/"
digna_COOKIE_SECURE = false
digna_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = true
digna_COOKIE_SAME_SITE = "lax"
digna_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN = 86400
digna_MAX_WORKERS = 4
Parameter Value Notes digna_FERNET_KEY Encryption key Used to encrypt tokens and cookies (default provided) digna_COOKIE_DOMAIN localhost Match your frontend domain digna_COOKIE_SECURE false (local) / true (production) Use true for HTTPS connections digna_COOKIE_HTTPONLY true Always enabled for security digna_COOKIE_SAME_SITE lax Prevents CSRF attacks digna_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN 86400 (24 hours) Session timeout in seconds digna_MAX_WORKERS Number of CPU cores - 1 Number of parallel inspection tasks

Tip

To find the number of CPU cores available on your Mac, run sysctl -n hw.ncpu.

docs.title: [logging] Section
docs.text:
This section configures logging behavior:

[logging]
digna_LOGGING_MODE = "INFO"
digna_LOGGING_BACKUP_COUNT = 10
